questions.stem: Quick-closing valves on fuel tanks let the crew:
options: Increase fuel flow to the engine
Shut off fuel supply from a position outside the machinery space
Drain water from the tank bottom
questions.explanation: In an engine-room fire you must be able to stop fuel without entering the space.

questions.stem: An alarm that sounds before a fixed engine-room smothering system discharges is there to:
options: Warn people to leave and make sure everyone is accounted for
questions.explanation: The gas is dangerous to people, so the space must be evacuated and closed first.

questions.stem: Compared with a weathertight door, a watertight door is built to:
options: Prevent the spread of fire only
Keep out water under pressure when compartments flood
questions.explanation: Watertight doors maintain subdivision. Weathertight doors only keep out weather and spray.

questions.stem: Which machinery is normally stoppable from outside the engine room?
options: Main engines, fuel supply and ventilation fans
questions.explanation: Emergency stops outside the space let you shut down fuel and air feeding a fire.

questions.stem: On hearing the alarm that warns of fire-extinguishing gas discharge you should:
questions.explanation: The gas can displace breathable air, and the alarm is your only warning.

questions.stem: Which extinguisher type is NOT suitable for a live electrical fire?
questions.explanation: Water conducts electricity and can electrocute the user. Water also spreads burning oil. Use CO2 or dry chemical, and isolate the power if you can.

questions.stem: A carbon dioxide extinguisher is suitable for fires of:
questions.explanation: CO2 smothers flammable liquid fires and leaves no residue on electrical equipment. It is not effective on deep-seated Class A fires, and it displaces oxygen in small spaces.

questions.stem: When using a portable extinguisher you should aim at:
options: The base of the flames, sweeping side to side
questions.explanation: Attack the fuel at the base of the fire. PASS means pull the pin, aim, squeeze and sweep.

questions.stem: On your rounds, which check on a portable extinguisher is most useful?
options: That it is warm to the touch
That the gauge is in the green and the pin and seal are in place
That it is as heavy as it was last year
That it is painted the right colour
questions.explanation: A gauge in the green, an intact pin and seal, a clear hose and a bracket in the right place all show the unit is ready. It is serviced separately by a competent person.

questions.stem: Which sequence is correct before a fixed gas system is released into a machinery space?
options: Wait for the fire to die down, then discharge
Alarm, account for everyone, stop engines and fans, close openings, then discharge on the master's order
Discharge first, then call everyone out
questions.explanation: The gas is dangerous to people and works only in a sealed space. Everyone must be out and counted, and fuel, air and openings shut off before release.

questions.stem: After a fixed CO2 system has discharged, the space can be re-entered only when:
options: It has been ventilated and declared safe, with breathing apparatus if in doubt
The smoke has cleared at the door
questions.explanation: CO2 displaces air and can remain after the fire is out. Re-entry waits for cooling, ventilation and the master's confirmation.

questions.stem: Quick-closing valves are operated from outside the machinery space so that:
options: The fuel can be sampled easily
The tanks can be pumped dry
Fuel can be shut off without entering a space full of fire and smoke
questions.explanation: In a fire you must stop the fuel feeding it. The remote operation, usually by a wire or lever on deck, means nobody has to go in.

questions.stem: A watertight door at sea should normally be:
options: Left open to let air circulate
Kept closed except when someone is passing through, and never wedged open
questions.explanation: A watertight door only keeps the vessel subdivided if it is closed. A wedge defeats it, which would let flooding spread.

questions.stem: How should fire detectors, alarms and emergency stops be treated?
options: Tested regularly, with the checks recorded in the log
Disabled whenever they give a nuisance alarm
Left alone because they are the builder's responsibility
questions.explanation: Safety equipment only helps if it works, so it is tested on a schedule and the test is logged. Disabling a detector without permission removes the early warning, and waiting for a fire to test it is too late.
